name: BBQ Pineapple Flatbreads
desc: Flatbreads spread with BBQ sauce and topped with jammy onion and pineapple, poblano, and two cheeses, finished with pickled onion.

source.title: BBQ Pineapple Flatbreads with Caramelized & Pickled Onions
source.evidence: Identical ingredient list and amounts (4 oz pineapple, 5 tsp red wine vinegar, 4 oz fresh mozzarella, 4 tbsp BBQ sauce, 1/4 cup Monterey Jack, 1/4 oz cilantro) and the same 450°F method.

ingredients.raw: 1 medium red onion, halved and thinly sliced
4 oz canned pineapple chunks, drained, juice reserved
4 oz fresh mozzarella, diced into 1/2-inch pieces
1/4 oz fresh cilantro (about 1/4 cup leaves), finely chopped

steps: Place a foil-lined baking sheet on the top rack and preheat the oven to 450°F.
Quick-pickle the onion: Drain the pineapple over a small bowl, reserving the juice. Stir a quarter of the sliced onion, half the vinegar, and a pinch of salt into the juice. Set aside.
Heat a drizzle of the vegetable oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add the remaining onion and cook, stirring and adding splashes of water if it sticks, until softened, 6-8 minutes.
While the onion cooks, halve, core, and very thinly slice the poblano into strips. Toss the strips with the olive oil and a pinch each of salt and pepper.

Raise the heat under the onion to medium-high. Add the pineapple and another drizzle of vegetable oil and cook, stirring, until the pineapple is lightly browned, 2-3 minutes. Stir in the remaining vinegar and cook until the onion and pineapple are jammy, 1-2 minutes more. Season with salt and pepper.

Rub each flatbread with the remaining vegetable oil. Carefully take the hot baking sheet out and set the flatbreads on it. Spread with the BBQ sauce, then top with the onion and pineapple, poblano, Monterey Jack, and mozzarella.
Bake on the top rack until the cheese melts and the edges are golden brown, 10-12 minutes.
Top with the cilantro and the drained pickled onion, cut into pieces, and serve.
